waf_rulesets: Enable Cloudflare OWASP Core Ruleset (CRS) with anomaly scoring threshold 40+ to block SQL injection, XSS, RFI, LFI, and command injection attacks targeting API routes. Deploy Cloudflare Managed Ruleset for API protection to enforce JSON payload validation and schema enforcement on /api/v1/*, /api/v2/*, /api/v3/* endpoints — complements the existing 2MB body cap in api/index.js:9 and MAX_INPUT_CHARS=12000 in rate_limiter.py:34. Enable Cloudflare Bot Fight Mode and Super Bot Fight Mode to block credential stuffing against /admin/auth/google and /admin/auth/config endpoints. Configure Cloudflare WAF custom rules to: (1) block requests missing CF-Connecting-IP header to prevent direct IP bypass, (2) enforce User-Agent presence for public API paths, (3) block known-scanner signatures (e.g., 'sqlmap', 'nikto') targeting astrology/interpretation endpoints, (4) rate-limit /api/v1/telegram/webhook to prevent Telegram webhook spoofing. The existing admin_auth_middleware (main.py:194-205) provides Google OAuth layer-7 auth; WAF adds layer-3/4/7 pre-filtering before requests reach HF backend, reducing origin load from 10 RPM per-IP quota to near-zero for automated scanners.
turnstile_value: Cloudflare Turnstile complements (not replaces) the existing Google OAuth admin authentication. Current architecture: admin routes use Google OAuth bearer token verification (main.py:163-191) calling oauth2.googleapis.com/tokeninfo per request — stateless but adds ~8ms latency per admin API call. Turnstile deployment points: (1) Embed Turnstile widget in the Vercel static frontend (horo-consultant-psi.vercel.app) for the /admin and /hitl-studio UIs — this stops automated credential-stuffing and brute-force against admin panels without requiring Google auth for every page navigation; (2) Add Turnstile challenge on /admin/auth/google endpoint before OAuth flow begins — prevents bot-driven OAuth callback spam; (3) Deploy invisible Turnstile on /api/v1/telegram/webhook endpoint to verify legitimate Telegram-originated requests. Turnstile adds value by: blocking automated bot traffic at edge before it consumes RateLimiter quota (10 RPM per IP); protecting static admin UI paths that currently have NO bot protection (admin.html served from HF Space with only bearer token check); reducing Google tokeninfo API calls by filtering obvious bots at CF edge. Keep Google OAuth bearer token for authorization of actual admin API mutations — Turnstile is pre-auth bot filtering, Google OAuth remains the authorization layer.
rate_limiting_strategy: Current RateLimiter (rate_limiter.py) is in-application token-bucket with: DDoS micro-burst 5 RPS, per-IP 10 RPM, daily budget 40-150 req/day, monthly USD cap, 12K input cap, 1.2K output cap. Cloudflare Workers Rate Limiting differs fundamentally: (1) CF Workers rate limiting operates at edge PoPs BEFORE requests traverse the internet to HF Space — saves origin CPU/memory vs Python defaultdict-based in-memory tracking; (2) CF rate limits use global counter store (not per-instance in-memory) — critical since HF Spaces may run multiple workers losing shared state; (3) CF Workers supports unauthenticated (free plan) and authenticated tiers with adaptive limits per path/role; (4) CF supports session-based identification (cookies/headers) vs current IP-only tracking (main.py:221 uses request.client.host with no X-Forwarded-For awareness behind Vercel proxy). Migration strategy: move DDoS micro-burst protection (5 RPS) to Cloudflare L3/L4/L7 DDoS protection (automatic, unlimited) and Cloudflare Rate Limiting Rules for per-IP quotas — this reduces HF Space CPU load from token-bucket computation. Keep application-layer daily budget (40-150 req/day) and monthly USD cap in RateLimiter because: (a) daily/monthly windows are long-duration counters better suited to persistent state, (b) cost-billing integration (monthly_budget_cap_usd) requires application-level cost tracking unavailable in CF edge rules, (c) input/output clamping is semantic request validation not network-layer rate limiting. Cloudflare Workers Rate Limiting is stateless and cannot enforce character/token caps. Recommended hybrid: CF Rate Limiting Rule at 100 req/min per IP (10x headroom above app 10 RPM) with Challenge action; app RateLimiter remains as authoritative 10 RPM + daily budget + cost guard. Use CF IP Access Rules to block known bad IPs at edge, reducing noise before app-layer processing.
architecture_benefits: Adding Cloudflare in front of the Vercel→HF Space architecture yields defense-in-depth across 7 layers: (1) Cloudflare DNS (CNAME flattening at apex) replaces Vercel DNS dependency, enabling orange-cloud proxy for DDoS protection; (2) Cloudflare L3/L4/L7 DDoS mitigation absorbs volumetric attacks (SYN floods, UDP amplification) that would otherwise saturate HF Space bandwidth — current app has NO L3/L4 protection; (3) Cloudflare WAF managed rulesets (OWASP CRS + API protection) block OWASP Top-10 attacks before reaching Vercel gateway (api/index.js) or HF backend, reducing the 12K input char clamping load; (4) Cloudflare Bot Fight Mode blocks automated scanners that currently consume RateLimiter quota (10 RPM/IP) and trigger 429s that waste HF CPU cycles; (5) Cloudflare Turnstile adds invisible bot detection for /admin and /admin/auth/google, complementing Google OAuth bearer auth with pre-auth filtering; (6) Cloudflare Workers Rate Limiting at edge offloads the token-bucket computation from HF Space Python process — current rate_limiter.py:143-144 maintains defaultdict in-memory state per worker; (7) Cloudflare IP Access Rules and Custom Rules enforce geo-blocking (if needed for Thai market focus), ASN blocking for known-bad hosting providers, and CF-Connecting-IP enforcement to prevent direct HF Space IP bypass (critical: HF Space URL pphothidaen-horoconsultant-core-backend.hf.space is exposed in vercel.json:28, enabling attackers to bypass Vercel gateway and all its CORS/validation). Architecture change: Vercel→HF becomes Vercel→Cloudflare→HF, with Cloudflare as the security perimeter. Supabase RLS remains untouched (layer-8 data security). Doppler secrets store remains untouched (layer-9 secrets management). Docker non-root (UID 1000) on HF remains the container-level safeguard. The existing multi-tier security (CORS at api/index.js:297-306, path validation at api/index.js:68-101, method enforcement at api/index.js:103-113, bearer check at api/index.js:119-127) is preserved and augmented by Cloudflare pre-filtering.
